screenshots.verdict: Not shippable yet. I checked the images directly: all 11 screens are exactly 2868x1320 with no alpha. Every frame is real gameplay, and the style (navy band, white headline in Kenney Future, amber sub-line) is the same across the set. Headlines are short and readable at 600 px. Frame 03 (skywritten SKILL ISSUE!) and alt_3 (the six-world strip) are the strongest images. The main problem is frame 01, which has to sell the app in one second and doesn't: at 600 px it reads as a volcano landscape with a blue plane. The red enemy is a thin end-on sliver hidden behind the crosshair, there are no visible tracers, and the sub-line repeats "friends". The 97%-opaque band lets ghost HUD text show through (stats row, lives, kill feed), and a kill-feed line ("Kabir shot down Riya") sits fully legible just under the band. A top art director would reject that as dirty. The touch-control circles cover about 25% of every full-bleed frame. Frame 04 has a mirrored, backwards "PAYBACK TIME" skywrite. Frame 05's LOCK box is tiny at phone size, and its sub-line claims bombs and flares that aren't in the frame. In frame 06 the snow panel is weak and the lightning reads as a white smear. The two inset menu frames (02, 07) have small text on a busy blurred background. The 2622x1206 set does not exist yet.
fixes: Frame 01, aso/creative/raw/sel_dogfight_lan.png via aso/tools/capture_scenes.gd (lan scene): re-capture a tighter dogfight. Put the red enemy plane 40-80 m ahead, side-on or banking (not end-on), with tracers clearly visible hitting it, and enemy plus your plane filling about 40% of the frame height. The volcano can stay as the backdrop but should not be the subject. Pick the take where the conflict reads at 600 px wide.

Frame 01 copy, aso/tools/compose_screens.gd SET: the sub-line 'Aeroplane fights with friends' repeats the headline. Replace it with a fact that adds information, e.g. 'Online or LAN. Up to 8 pilots.' Keep the India keyword ('AEROPLANE FIGHTS WITH FRIENDS') as the separate PPO headline variant the storyboard already plans, not as a sub-line.

aso/tools/compose_screens.gd _band(): ghost HUD text (stats row, lives, kill feed, II/CAM/TAUNT/TEAM/MAP buttons) shows through the 0.97/0.95 navy band, and the last kill-feed line ('Kabir shot down Riya', frames 03 and first_alt_1, also visible in 04/05) sits legible in the fade zone. Make the band's solid part fully opaque (alpha 1.0) and extend it past the kill feed. Better still, add a capture flag in aso/tools/capture_scenes.gd that hides the top HUD row and kill feed before the frame is taken, so nothing has to be covered.

Hiding is still real gameplay, and it gives the art much more room.

Frame 04, raw/sel_ai_battle.png: the skywritten 'PAYBACK TIME!' is seen from behind, so it reads mirrored and backwards on the right, which looks like a bug. I checked all 11 PNGs in creative/screens/: each is 2868x1320 RGB with no alpha (MEASURED with sips). Every frame is a real capture and every copy claim has a source. There are no Top Gun callsigns in frame; 04 shows "Kite" and "Pepper", checked on full-res crops. The strongest images are 01 and 03, plus first_alt_1 and first_alt_2. The craft problems: every frame uses the same plain navy band, which looks like a dev template. The sub-lines are too small to read in the phone store. 04, 05 and 06 have weak or cluttered subjects. Two of the seven frames are dense menu UI. Debug-looking world labels ("Balloon", "SUPPLY 691m", target rings) are still on screen. screenshots.verdict: I checked the specs and they pass. All 11 frames are exactly 2868x1320, RGB, no alpha (checked with sips and the PNG header). The 2622x1206 copies are correct and none is older than its source. The set is honest real gameplay with one exception: the 3x lock box in 05. The style is consistent and 03 (SKILL ISSUE! over the volcano) is close to agency quality. It is not yet shippable by a top agency, for six reasons. (1) The headline font is very wide with very wide letter spacing and runs edge to edge. At phone size the R reads like an A and the N and M look lowercase ('FAIEnDS', 'mORLDS'), so a headline takes longer than a second to read. (2) The same dogfight capture appears in 01, 02, first_alt_2 and ppo_in_aeroplane, so frames 1 and 2 of the gallery repeat the same image. (3) 05 is the weakest frame: it is cluttered, shows stray name tags and a cut-off HUD piece, the target is hard to make out, it shows no rocket, and its HUD is enlarged (Guideline 2.3 risk). (4) In 02 and 07 the left panels look like debug UI or are half empty, and the headline runs across the split line. (5) The game's own variety never appears: no Capture the Flag, Base Assault, AA guns or SAMs, co-op, bombs or explosions. (6) 01 hooks well enough but does not show 'friends' (nothing marks the red plane as a person), and a pale yellow fire glow at the left edge looks like a rendering glitch.
fixes: aso/tools/compose_screens.gd HEAD_FONT/_label: the headline is hard to read at phone size. kenney_future_narrow with its wide spacing makes the R look like an A and the N and M look lowercase on contact_sheet_350.png. Switch the headline to a heavy, tightly spaced font that is already in the project (for example the bold menu font already used for the sub-line, set larger), or set tight letter spacing with FontVariation spacing_glyph < 0. Cap the headline width at about 75% of W instead of W-2*SAFE, so it reads as a block rather than a full-width banner. Keep the skywriting font only where it echoes the in-game skywriting (03, first_alt_1).

icons.verdict: The files meet Apple's technical requirements: all three icons are 1024x1024 RGB with no alpha, checked with sips. Only Concept A is close to shippable, and the set is not shippable as a whole. A reads as a plane at 60 px, has a strong silhouette and is clearly different from the blue icons in the category. Its weaknesses are the camera angle, which shows the plane's belly and landing gear, and the wing struts, which render as loose black sticks. B, the one the doc recommends, uses realistic fighter jets. The doc itself says that makes it blend in with 13 of 16 combat competitors, but the cub version it recommends was never rendered. B's red jet is a dark maroon with low contrast, and its tracers read as dashed ladder rungs. C is the same cub from almost the same three-quarter-below angle as A, so the three concepts are not really different. C also sits on the category's standard blue, uses a white outline the game never uses, and its island and cloud shrink to specks at 60 px. The contact sheet compares the concepts only with the current icon, not with the 20 competitor icons the doc promises, so the distinctiveness claim hasn't been tested. No dark or tinted variants exist.
fixes: aso/tools/render_icons.gd concept("B_duel"): change both plane("fighter", ...) calls to plane("cub", ...) and re-render. The doc's recommended launch icon (cubs on a warm background) does not exist yet, so the recommendation in aso/icon-concepts.md points at an image nobody can look at. Also replace the light-blue-to-peach gradient with a warm, non-blue background like A's, because the top half of the current B is still category blue.

render_icons.gd B_duel: the red plane renders as dark maroon (Color 1.0,0.35,0.3 under toon shading plus a back-lit sun) and almost disappears against the sky at 60 px. Rotate it so the lit side faces the camera, or set its sun or ambient light separately, and keep it at least 30% of the frame width as the doc's own rule says (it is about 25% now). There is also a thin bright-red fringe along the red jet's edges, at the right wingtip and nose. Check the outline shader or the halo blend on that plane.

render_icons.gd B_duel tracers: _halo() is built from the full foreground alpha, so the tracers get a thick ink outline and read as ladder rungs, not bullets. Draw the tracers after the halo and composite them without a stroke, or exclude them from the mask. Use 2 longer, tapered, glowing streaks per gun instead of 3 boxed dashes, starting right at the blue plane's nose so the shooter is obvious at 60 px.

render_icons.gd concept("C_toyworld"): it is the same cub at nearly the same angle and scale as A (A rotation 18,-24,-22; C rotation 22,-30,-18), so the set has two concepts, not three. Make C actually different. For example, a head-on, nose-to-camera cub with a big spinning prop filling 90% of the frame (a character face shot), or a 3-plane squad formation for the co-op/friends angle. If the world idea stays, make the island at least 35% of the frame. A 7.0 radius at 80 units depth currently covers about 12% and becomes a 6 px green blob at 60 px.

render_icons.gd C_toyworld: change stroke from [12, Color(1,1,1)] to the game's dark INK outline, as in A and B. The white sticker outline doesn't appear anywhere in the game's art, so it fails the 'matches real game art' check. Replace the saturated mid-blue gradient (0.14,0.4,0.92 to 0.72,0.9,1.0) with the Sky Kingdom lavender/deep-blue palette described in the doc, or with a warm sky. Right now C joins the 13/20 blue icons.

Wing struts in A and C (the cub's _box struts in planes.gd, drawn with ink by outline.gdshader) render as loose black diagonal sticks over the wing and fuselage, and look like scratches at 120 px and below. In render_icons.gd plane(), hide the strut meshes after Planes.build/dress for icon renders (find them by the strut material or by name), or scale them up about 2x.

render_icons.gd A_hero camera: the camera (-5,-2.2,-16.5) looks up at the belly, so the wheels and gear legs are the strongest shapes and the cabin and canopy, the plane's 'face', are hidden. Move the camera above the wing plane (positive y) so the canopy, cowling and top of the wing show, keep about a 20 degree bank, and keep the prop blades visible. Use sticker 6 (Shark Mouth) on the nose instead of sticker 1. The star is a few pixels on the fin and disappears below 180 px.

render_icons.gd A_hero background: the bright spot (u 0.42, v 0.36) is off-centre from the plane, which makes the right and bottom heavy and muddy orange. Centre the hotspot behind the fuselage, and consider a darker vignette edge so the blue plane's silhouette pops when Apple's mask cuts the corners.

aso/tools/icon_sheet.gd / icon_sheet.sh: add a row of the 20 competitor icons, and show each concept at 60 px inside a mock App Store search row next to them, as promised in step 2 of aso/icon-concepts.md. Right now the distinctiveness claims ('most different from the competitor row') rest on comparison with the current icon only. Also add 40 px and 29 px sizes (Spotlight and Settings).

Produce the dark and tinted variants the doc mentions: in render_icons.gd, add a bg option for near-black and a grayscale pass for the chosen concept, writing *_dark.png and *_tinted.png to aso/creative/icons/. Otherwise Apple auto-generates versions from a gradient that nobody has checked.

aso/icon-concepts.md: update the 'Current draft render' notes after re-rendering, and label the 60 px readability results MEASURED from the sheet. The current C note estimates the 60 px result even though the contact sheet already shows it. State plainly that the recommended B-with-cubs icon is unrendered until it is.

icons.verdict: Not shippable yet. The technical specs pass: all 5 icons are 1024x1024 RGB with no alpha (checked with sips -g hasAlpha). The art is honest: the planes come from Planes.build with the game's toon shader and ink outline, and the warm backgrounds do break up the row of blue competitor icons on the contact sheet. The craft is still below the agency bar. B (the recommended icon) leaves most of the canvas as pale empty peach. Its planes are each about a third of the frame wide, and its tracers fade out at 60 px, so at real store size the 'dogfight' story it was chosen for is mostly gone. A has the strongest silhouette, but the camera is high and nearly top-down, so it reads as a flat blue X: the white cowling and prop wash into the pale-yellow centre, and the dangling wheel and rocket rods add clutter. C is a draft: an orange cowling blob, a brown prop that dominates the frame, a gas-bag pod cut off at the top-right edge that reads as a stray cream blob, a black cockpit hole, gear sticks, and a wing cropped flat along the top. A and B use the same plane, palette and ink treatment, so only two of the three concepts are really different directions, and the third one is weak. There is also a continuity gap: the Toy Cub in builds/appstore/1-battle.png has yellow wings on a blue fuselage, while every icon shows an all-blue cub.
fixes: aso/tools/render_icons.gd, concept B_duel: make the planes bigger and overlap the duel. Move the red foe closer along `dir` (use about 9 instead of `dir * 15.0`) and raise fit[1] from 0.86 to about 0.98, so the planes together fill the square and each one spans at least 45% of the width. aso/tools/render_icons.gd, B_duel shots: make the tracers survive 60 px. Extend the second segment to `g.lerp(t, 0.95)` so the fire actually reaches the red plane, raise the widths from 18/22 to about 30/40, and add a small hit spark or smoke puff at the impact point on the red plane (a spark at the end of `_tracer`, or one extra radial blob in `_compose`). At 60 px the tracers are currently a faint yellow smudge that stops short of the target.

aso/tools/render_icons.gd, B_duel bg: the centre stop Color(1.0, 0.94, 0.66) is close to the cream wingtips (STYLE[0].trim 0.95,0.93,0.85), so the tips of both planes fade into it. Deepen the gradient (centre around (1.0, 0.78, 0.4), edges around (0.85, 0.3, 0.25)), or move its centre away from where the planes sit, so the cream tips and the blue plane separate cleanly.

aso/tools/render_icons.gd, concept A_hero: lower the camera from (-11, 6, -12) to about (-9, 2.5, -13) and widen the shot (fov around 45, then refit) so the nose and prop come toward the viewer and the plane reads as a chunky three-quarter toy, not a flat top-down X. aso/tools/render_icons.gd, A_hero: the white cowling and prop sit on the brightest part of the radial (centre Color(1.0,0.92,0.52)), so the face of the plane disappears. Move the radial centre behind the wing, or darken the centre, so the cowling has contrast. Also make the Shark Mouth sticker read: scale or position it so it is more than a 2 px red dot at 60 px, or drop it.

aso/tools/render_icons.gd, concept C_face: re-render it or replace it. The Sky Kingdom trim (0.86,0.64,0.25) makes the cowling an orange blob, the dark prop blades dominate, the gas-bag pod is cut by the top-right edge, and the wing is chopped flat along the top. Lower fit[1] from 0.9 to about 0.75 so both wingtips sit inside the square, use world 0 (no pods; cream cowling) or hide the pod nodes, set prop_deg so the blades form a clean X, and keep the cockpit glass visible as a face rather than a black hole. Then check it at 40 px.

aso/tools/render_icons.gd: make the three concepts different directions, not one look repeated. A and B share the plane, the warm radial palette and the ink. research.verdict: Strong, honest research. The evidence holds up: every number I spot-checked matched aso/data or a fresh API call. strategy.verdict: Solid, well-sourced work, but not shippable yet. I ran the validator on all four strategy listings and every one exits 0. strategy.verdict:
This is solid, honest work but not yet shippable at top-agency level. I ran the validator myself: listings A, A_en-US, B and C all exit 0 with 0 FAIL. B has 1 WARN for its "air war" name, and listing_current fails as expected. I checked about 30 feature claims against the code and nearly all hold, including:
- 8 players (main.gd:4) and 5-character codes (rooms.gd CODE_CHARS)
- the 15-second revive beacon, the 24 taunts and the 6 AI archetypes (ai.gd)
- 2v2, 4v4 and 6v6 team sizes (SIZES per team, main.gd:2038), CTF first to 3 (CAPS_TO_WIN), 20 Free Flight balloons, and a 3-bomber escort over 8 waves
- the Twin Guns, Shield and Rocket Swarm power-ups, Restore Purchases (shop_ui.gd:48), the offline solo peer, and the touch options for tilt, auto-fire, left-handed play and vibration
- per-world plane gear (floats, skis, tyres), 6 music tracks, and the Team Dogfight human-per-team rule (main.gd:909)
- the LAN option on iOS, including the NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription entry

No trademarks appear in the keywords, and there are no claims of upgrades or progression that don't exist.

Four things hold it back:
1. The "Sim" decision is argued for but never made in the shipping files.
2. Indexed fields still carry expectation risks: "Sim", "online" and "Flight".
3. India's strongest honest angle, offline play, is missing from every keyword field.
4. B is a strawman: its name copies a competitor's title. Also, the recommendation of A over C cuts against the review evidence the doc itself presents (ads complaints 68 and fun/simple praise 61, against 14 asking for friends play).
fixes: data/listing_A.json, listing_A_en-US.json, listing_C.json: make the 'drop Sim' call in the files instead of leaving it as an open option. Set name to 'Toy Plane Dogfight' (A) and 'Toy Plane Arcade' (C), re-run validate_metadata.py and coverage.py, and update the positioning.md Short version table, which still says 'Toy Plane Sim: Dogfight (or ...)'. The doc's own evidence (game-audit §2 says no flight model; 'simulator' terms scored relevance 1-2) calls 'Sim' a 2.3 expectation mismatch, yet every listing still ships it. C's 'Sim: Flight Arcade' doubles down with 'Flight'.

data/listing_A.json and listing_A_en-US.json keywords: remove 'online' (7 bytes). There is no public lobby or matchmaking (rooms.gd:4-6). positioning.md already removed 'online' from screenshot headline 4 for exactly this 2.3 reason, so keeping it as an indexed term aimed at 'online plane game' (IN top-5 median 99,850 ratings, 0 autocomplete) is inconsistent and draws searchers who will write 'nobody online' reviews. Replace it with 'offline' (see next fix) or 'pvp' ('pvp games' is autocomplete #1 in both stores, keyword-research row 38).

data/listing_C.json and listing_A.json keywords: add 'offline'. keyword-research.md line 10 records 'aeroplane games offline' as an IN autocomplete hint, and solo play really runs on OfflineMultiplayerPeer (main.gd:264-279). C's whole promise ('no internet') sits in no indexed field. For C, drop 'friends' (it contradicts C's solo focus and is covered weakly anyway) or 'sky' to make room. For A India, use the 7 spare bytes (93/100) plus the bytes freed by removing 'online'.
data/listing_A_en-US.json description: change 'armour' to 'armor'. The US localization was copy-pasted from en-GB.

positioning.md Recommendation: the evidence favours C as the default. C answers the larger review themes (ads 68 and fun/simple 61, against friends 14), and A's headline depends on free public MQTT brokers including test.mosquitto.org, which documents itself as experimental, with no TURN relay. Either flip the order to 'ship C; switch to A once the Jio/Airtel join test reaches at least 9 of 10 and a hosted broker exists', or state plainly that A is chosen on differentiation and the existing draft (sunk cost), not on evidence. Also add the 8-phone room as a TestFlight check before promo text says 'up to 8 pilots'. MAX_PLAYERS=8 is verified but 8 mobile peers over a WebRTC star is untested.

data/listing_B.json: replace the strawman name 'Toy Plane Sim: Air War', which the validator flags for copying 'Alliance: Air War' (2.3.7/4.1), with a compliant name such as 'Toy Plane Dogfight' and a combat subtitle, or 'Toy Plane: Fighter Battles'. In positioning.md, either give C a distinct keyword set (offline, arcade, simple, sky, bomber, shooter, pvp) or state openly that A and C differ only in subtitle, promo text and screenshots.

strategy.verdict:
The research is solid and the copy is honest, but this is not yet shippable by an agency standard. I ran tools/validate_metadata.py on every listing: A, A_en-US, B, C and C_en-US all give 0 FAIL and 0 WARN with exit 0, the same as the appendix. Only listing_current.json fails, as expected. I checked about 30 feature claims against the code and they hold: 24 taunts including 'Skill issue!', 'GG!' and 'Nice flying!' (taunts.gd:7-16); a 15 s beacon (main.gd:18); 3 escort bombers and 8 waves (main.gd:25,1072); 20 Free Flight balloons (main.gd:1067); first to 3 flags (objectives.gd:14); Twin Guns, Shield and Rocket Swarm (plane.gd:275); plane stats (planes.gd:9-12); floats, skis and tyres (planes.gd:30-33); six AI archetypes with the named moves (ai.gd:24-31); 2v2 to 6v6 per side (main.gd:2748); one music track per world (assets/music); tilt, auto-fire, left-handed, vibration and resize (touch.gd); Try-in-Free-Flight and Restore Purchases (shop_ui.gd:44,48); solo play offline through BATTLE VS AI with the mode picker (main.gd:265-279,2432,2507). There are no trademarks in any keyword field.

The problems:
1. The recommended listing breaks the doc's own honesty rule. It says 'up to 8 pilots' while the doc says no listing may say that until an 8-phone test passes.
2. The highest-weight fields are underused. The name uses 16 of 30 characters and spends 'Arcade' on a word with 0 measured autocomplete.
3. Keyword bytes go to P3 terms while P1 and P2 terms go uncovered.
4. The 'ads' evidence behind C is concentrated in hypercasual apps and is zero among the combat games C actually competes with.
5. A and C are by the author's own admission not separate keyword strategies.
6. The store name will not match the name on the device and in the game, and the doc treats that as an open item rather than a blocker.
fixes: aso/data/listing_C.json, listing_C_en-US.json, listing_B.json, listing_A.json and listing_A_en-US.json: remove 'for up to 8 pilots' from C and B and 'Up to 8 pilots per room' from A. In A's promo text, change 'and up to 8 pilots fly in one sky' to 'and your friends fly in one sky'. positioning.md lines 192 and 431 say no listing may say '8' until the 8-phone test passes (main.gd:4 MAX_PLAYERS is untested), yet the recommended launch listing C says it. That is a self-identified Guideline 2.3 accuracy risk. Also add 'up to 8 | warn | 8-phone room untested (positioning.md check 3)' to aso/data/banned_terms.txt so the validator catches it.

aso/positioning.md, Decision 1, and the Recommendation: make the name mismatch a launch blocker, not an open item. project.godot:13 config/name, export_presets.cfg:41 product_name, the main menu title (main.gd:2427-2428 'TOY PLANE' / 'SIM'), PRIVACY.md and SUPPORT.md all say 'Toy Plane Sim'. App Review often rejects when the store name and the on-device name do not match. Either change those before submitting 'Toy Plane Arcade', or keep the store name close to the device name. Also add a WARN to tools/validate_metadata.py when the listing name's first words differ from project.godot config/name.

aso/data/listing_C.json and listing_C_en-US.json, keywords: replace ',capture,flag' (13 bytes, covers only the P3 term 'capture the flag') with ',combat,fighting' (16 bytes). India goes from 97 to 100 bytes. This covers the P1 term 'plane fighting game' and the rel-5 P2 terms 'air combat' and 'air combat games' (MEASURED: coverage.py lists all three as missing for C). For en-US (98 bytes), drop 'sky' (P2 only through 'sky war' and 'sky battle', both US autocomplete 1) along with capture and flag so the swap fits. Re-run coverage.py and record the new P1 and P2 counts in positioning.md.

aso/data/listing_C*.json, name field: 'Toy Plane Arcade' uses 16 of 30 characters in the most heavily weighted field, and 'arcade' has 0 autocomplete in both stores (keywords.json: 'arcade plane game' P3, 0/0). Test a name that carries a P1 or P2 term in the 14 spare characters, for example 'Toy Plane Arcade: Air Combat' (28) or 'Toy Plane: Air War Arcade'. Check that the validator's competitor-title check stays clean (it flagged 'air war' before). Then remove the duplicated words from the keyword field and use the freed bytes for '3d' or 'shooting'. Do the same for A's 'Toy Plane Dogfight' (18/30).

aso/positioning.md, Recommendation point 1 and the Strategy C evidence block: report that 60 of the 79 'ads' matches come from two hypercasual apps (Epic Plane Evolution 35, Sling Plane 3D 25) and 9 from Airline Commander. Every combat competitor C actually fights for 'aeroplane game' and 'fighter plane game' (Metalstorm, Sky Warriors, War Thunder Mobile, Air Wings) has 0 ads complaints (MEASURED, data/review_theme_counts.txt). As written, '9.4% of reviews' overstates how well 'no ads' fits C's searchers. aso/positioning.md, Strategies section: the rubric asks for three genuinely different strategies, and the doc concedes A and C share 16 of 21 indexed words. aso/positioning.md, Strategy C 'New captures needed': the recommended launch listing has no rendered hero frame. 'NO ADS. JUST DOGFIGHTS.' and the balloons frame do not exist yet, and the first screenshot drives most of the conversion.
